sentences.chinese: 苻登藉烏合犬羊，偷存假息，料其智勇，非至尊之匹。
sentences.literal: Fu Deng, relying on a mob mixed as dogs and sheep, furtively preserves a false respite; gauge his wit and courage—they are no match for the most exalted.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng clings to a rabble no better than sheep, stealing breath on borrowed time; set his mind and mettle against yours, and he cannot rival the throne.

sentences.chinese: 霸王之起，必有驅除，然後克定大業。
sentences.literal: When a hegemon-king rises, there must be driving-off and clearing-away; only afterward can the great enterprise be settled.
sentences.idiomatic: The rise of every conqueror clears the field of rivals; only then can the great work stand complete.

sentences.chinese: 昔漢、魏之興也，皆十有餘年，乃能一同於海內，五六年間未為久也。
sentences.literal: In old days the rise of Han and of Wei each took more than ten years before they could unify within the seas; five or six years is not to be reckoned long.
sentences.idiomatic: The Han and the Wei each needed more than a decade to knit the realm into one. A span of five or six years is scarcely long to wait.

sentences.chinese: 主上神略內明，英武外發，可謂無敵於天下耳，取登有餘力。
sentences.literal: The sovereign's divine designs shine inward; heroic martial prowess issues outward—he may be called without peer under Heaven. Taking Deng leaves strength to spare.
sentences.idiomatic: Our lord reads the field in silence and strikes with open might; none under Heaven can stand before him. Fu Deng would fall and still leave force in reserve.

sentences.chinese: 願布德行仁，招賢納士，厲兵秣馬，以候天機。
sentences.literal: I pray you spread virtue and enact benevolence, summon worthies and accept knights, sharpen weapons and feed horses, and await Heaven's turning moment.
sentences.idiomatic: Spread humanity, gather the able, hone the blades, rest the steeds, and watch for the hour fate tilts your way.

sentences.chinese: 如其鴻業不成者，詵請腰斬以謝明公。
sentences.literal: If thus the great swan enterprise does not succeed, Shen asks to be cut at the waist to apologize to the enlightened duke.
sentences.idiomatic: If that high design fails, I, Shen, beg to be halved at the waist to answer to you.

sentences.chinese: 」緯言之於萇，萇大悅，賜詵爵關內侯。
sentences.literal: " Wei reported this to Chang; Chang was greatly pleased and bestowed on Shen the rank of marquis within the passes.
sentences.idiomatic: Wei relayed it to Yao Chang, who was delighted and enfeoffed Shen as a marquis within the passes.

sentences.chinese: 雷惡地率眾降萇，拜為鎮東將軍。
sentences.literal: Lei Ede led his host to surrender to Chang and was appointed General Who Guards the East.
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Ede brought his troops over to Yao Chang, who named him General Who Guards the East.

sentences.chinese: 魏褐飛自稱大將軍、沖天王，率氐胡數萬人攻安北姚當城於杏城，雷惡地應之，攻鎮東姚漢得于李潤。
sentences.literal: Wei Hefei styled himself Grand General and Heaven-Rushing King; he led tens of thousands of Di and Hu to attack Defender of the North Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng. Lei Ede answered him and struck General Who Guards the East Yao Hande at Lirun.
sentences.idiomatic: The rebel Wei Hefei declared himself Grand General and King Who Charges Heaven, then drove tens of thousands of Di and Hu against Yao Dangcheng at Xingcheng. Lei Ede joined the move and hit Yao Hande at Lirun.

sentences.chinese: 萇議將討之，群臣咸曰：「陛下不憂六十里苻登，乃憂六百里褐飛？
sentences.literal: Chang deliberated on campaigning against them. The assembled officials all said: "Your Majesty does not fret over Fu Deng sixty li away, yet frets over Hefei six hundred li away?"
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang weighed a punitive march. His ministers said: "You lose no sleep over Fu Deng on your doorstep, but lose it over Hefei far down the road?"

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「登非可卒殄，吾城亦非登所能卒圖。
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "Deng cannot be snuffed out in a stroke, nor can my stronghold be taken from him in a stroke."
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang replied: "Fu Deng will not vanish overnight, and my walls will not fall to him overnight either."

sentences.chinese: 惡地多智，非常人也。
sentences.literal: Ede abounds in schemes; he is no ordinary man.
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Ede is cunning—no common soldier of fortune.

sentences.chinese: 南引褐飛，東結董成，甘言美說以成奸謀，若得杏城、李潤，惡地據之，控制遠近，相為羽翼，長安東北非復吾有。
sentences.literal: Southward he draws Hefei; eastward he binds Dong Cheng; with honeyed words he finishes treasonous plots. If he holds Xingcheng and Lirun, Ede will sit on them, command near and far, and pair wing to wing—then the northeast of Chang'an is no longer ours.
sentences.idiomatic: He pulls Hefei from the south, ropes in Dong Cheng from the east, and sweet-talks his way through treason. Seize Xingcheng and Lirun and Lei Ede commands the approaches; wings locked, the northeast of Chang'an slips from our grasp.

sentences.chinese: 」於是潛軍赴之。
sentences.literal: " Thereupon he moved his army in secret and hurried to them.
sentences.idiomatic: So he stole a march with hidden troops.

sentences.chinese: 萇時眾不滿二千，褐飛、惡地眾至數萬，氐胡赴之者首尾不絕。
sentences.literal: At that time Chang's men numbered fewer than two thousand; Hefei's and Ede's ran to tens of thousands, and Di and Hu who flocked to them came in an unbroken train.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang had fewer than two thousand men; Hefei and Lei Ede mustered tens of thousands, with Di and Hu pouring in without end.

sentences.chinese: 萇每見一軍至，輒有喜色。
sentences.literal: Whenever Chang saw another host arrive, he showed a joyful face.
sentences.idiomatic: Each time fresh rebels appeared, Yao Chang looked glad.

sentences.chinese: 群下怪而問之，萇曰：「今同惡相濟，皆來會集，吾得乘勝席捲，一舉而覆其巢穴，東北無復餘也。
sentences.literal: His subordinates marveled and asked him. Chang said: "Now evildoers aid one another and gather in one place; I may ride victory and roll them up like a mat, overturn their nest in one stroke, and leave nothing left in the northeast."
sentences.idiomatic: His officers wondered aloud. Yao Chang said: "They flock together—traitors feeding traitors. I can sweep them in one rush, tear out the nest, and clear the whole northeast."

sentences.chinese: 」褐飛等以萇兵少，盡眾來攻。
sentences.literal: " Hefei and the others, because Chang's troops were few, brought their entire force to attack.
sentences.idiomatic: Thinking Yao Chang weak, Hefei threw every man forward.

sentences.chinese: 萇固壘不戰，示之以弱，潛遣子崇率騎數百，出其不意，以乘其後。
sentences.literal: Chang held fast behind his ramparts and would not fight, showing weakness; secretly he sent his son Chong with several hundred horse to slip out unlooked-for and strike their rear.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang hugged his walls and feigned frailty, while his son Chong looped behind with a few hundred riders and hit them where they did not look.

sentences.chinese: 褐飛兵擾亂，萇遣鎮遠王超、平遠譚亮率步騎擊之，褐飛眾大潰，斬褐飛及首級萬餘。
sentences.literal: Hefei's troops were thrown into confusion. Chang sent Distant Pacifier Wang Chao and Far-Smoother Tan Liang with foot and horse to strike them; Hefei's host broke utterly. Hefei was beheaded, and more than ten thousand heads were taken.
sentences.idiomatic: Hefei's lines crumbled. Yao Chang sent Wang Chao and Tan Liang with mixed arms; the rebel army shattered. Hefei lost his head, and the tally passed ten thousand.

sentences.chinese: 惡地請降，萇待之如初。
sentences.literal: Ede asked to surrender; Chang treated him as before.
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Ede sued for peace, and Yao Chang welcomed him as if nothing had changed.

sentences.chinese: 惡地每謂人曰：「吾自言智勇所施，足為一時之傑。
sentences.literal: Ede often told people: "I have always said that where I apply wit and courage, I am enough to be a champion of the age."
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Ede used to say: "Where I bring mind and nerve, I am fit to stand among the heroes of the hour."

sentences.chinese: 校數諸雄，如吾之徒，皆應跨據一方，獸嘯千里。
sentences.literal: Measured against the warlords, men like me ought to stride across one region and roar like beasts for a thousand li.
sentences.idiomatic: Stack me against the lords of the age: my kind should hold a quarter of the map and make the wilds echo for a thousand li.

sentences.chinese: 遇姚公智力摧屈，是吾分也。
sentences.literal: Meeting Lord Yao, wit and strength were broken and bent—that is my portion.
sentences.idiomatic: Then I met Lord Yao, and mind and might alike were broken—that was simply my lot.

sentences.chinese: 」惡地猛毅清肅，不可幹以非義，嶺北諸豪皆敬憚之。
sentences.literal: " Ede was fierce, resolute, clear, and stern; he could not be moved by what was unjust. The chiefs north of the ridges all honored and feared him.
sentences.idiomatic: Lei Ede was grim, upright, and austere—no appeal to wrong could sway him. North of the passes every strongman respected and dreaded him.

sentences.chinese: 萇命其將當城于營處一柵孔中蒔樹一根，以旌戰功。
sentences.literal: Chang ordered his general Dangcheng to plant one tree in a gap of the palisade at the camp site, to mark the battle merit.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang told General Yao Dangcheng to set a single sapling in a hole in the stockade where they had camped, a living marker of the fight.

sentences.chinese: 歲餘，問之，城曰：「營所至小，已廣之矣。
sentences.literal: After more than a year he asked about it. Dangcheng said: "The camp ground was extremely small; I have already enlarged it."
sentences.idiomatic: A year later he inquired. Dangcheng said: "The plot was tiny—I have widened it."

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「少來鬥戰無如此快，以千六百人破三萬眾，國之事業，由此克舉。
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "Since youth I have never known fighting so brisk. With sixteen hundred men we broke a host of thirty thousand; the state's enterprise, by this, could be raised."
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang said: "I have never had a quicker fight. Sixteen hundred broke thirty thousand; the kingdom's fate turned on that stroke."

sentences.chinese: 小乃為奇，大何足貴！」
sentences.literal: Small, then, is marvelous; what greatness is worth prizing!"
sentences.idiomatic: Small made the wonder—size would have cheapened it!"

sentences.chinese: 貳城胡曹寅、王達獻馬三千匹。
sentences.literal: The Hu of Ercheng, Cao Yin and Wang Da, presented three thousand horses.
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Yin and Wang Da, Hu leaders of Ercheng, brought three thousand horses as tribute.

sentences.chinese: 以寅為鎮北將軍、并州刺史，達鎮遠將軍、金城太守。
sentences.literal: Yin was made General Who Guards the North and Inspector of Bingzhou; Da was made General Who Distantly Pacifies and Administrator of Jincheng.
sentences.idiomatic: Cao Yin became General Who Guards the North and inspector of Bingzhou; Wang Da became General Who Distantly Pacifies and prefect of Jincheng.

sentences.chinese: 萇性簡率，群下有過，或面加罵辱。
sentences.literal: Chang's nature was plain and blunt; when subordinates erred, he sometimes reviled them to their faces.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang was rough and direct; when a follower slipped, he might curse him to his face.

sentences.chinese: 太常權翼言於萇曰：「陛下弘達自任，不修小節，駕馭群雄，苞羅俊異，棄嫌錄善，有高祖之量。
sentences.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Quan Yi said to Chang: "Your Majesty is magnanimous and trusts himself, does not fuss over small points, reins in the heroes, gathers the strange and excellent, casts aside old slights and records good deeds—you have Gaozu's measure.
sentences.idiomatic: Quan Yi, Minister of Ceremonies, told Yao Chang: "You are broad enough to trust your own judgment, above petty nicety; you harness warlords, gather odd talents, forgive old grudges and honor merit—you have the span of Han Gaozu.

sentences.chinese: 然輕慢之風，所宜除也。
sentences.literal: Yet the wind of slighting others is what ought to be removed.
sentences.idiomatic: Still, the habit of contempt is a thing you should shed.

sentences.chinese: 」萇曰：「吾之性也。
sentences.literal: " Chang said: "It is my nature."
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang answered: "That is simply how I am."

sentences.chinese: 吾於舜之美，未有片焉；
sentences.literal: As for Shun's perfections, I have not a scrap;
sentences.idiomatic: I own no shred of Shun's grace;

sentences.chinese: 漢祖之短，已收其一。
sentences.literal: of the Han founder's faults, I have already taken one.
sentences.idiomatic: but I have already pocketed one of the Han founder's vices.

sentences.chinese: 若不聞讜言，安知過也！」
sentences.literal: if I do not hear straight speech, how am I to know my faults!"
sentences.idiomatic: without blunt counsel, how would I ever see my own errors?"

sentences.chinese: 南羌竇鴦率戶五千來降，拜安西將軍。
sentences.literal: Dou Yang of the southern Qiang led five thousand households to surrender and was appointed General Who Pacifies the West.
sentences.idiomatic: Dou Yang of the southern Qiang came in with five thousand households; Yao Chang named him General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.chinese: 萇下書，有復私仇者，皆誅之。
sentences.literal: Chang issued an edict: whoever settled private blood-feuds would be executed.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang proclaimed: private vengeance would cost a man's life.

sentences.chinese: 將吏亡滅者，各隨所親以立後，振給長育之。
sentences.literal: For generals and clerks who had died, each according to kinship an heir was established, and they were succored and raised.
sentences.idiomatic: Fallen officers and clerks left heirs named by kin, and the state fed and reared them.

sentences.chinese: 鎮東苟曜據逆萬堡，密引苻登。
sentences.literal: General Who Guards the East Gou Yao held Rebel-Myriad Fort and secretly drew in Fu Deng.
sentences.idiomatic: Gou Yao, General Who Guards the East, held Niwang Fort and secretly opened the door to Fu Deng.

sentences.chinese: 萇與登戰，敗于馬頭原，收眾復戰。
sentences.literal: Chang fought Deng, was defeated at Matou Plain, gathered his host, and fought again.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang met Fu Deng, lost on Matou Plain, regrouped, and struck again.

sentences.chinese: 姚碩德謂諸將曰：「上慎于輕戰，每欲以計取之。
sentences.literal: Yao Shuo De said to the generals: "The sovereign is wary of rash battle; he always wishes to take the enemy by stratagem."
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Shuo De told his captains: "Our lord hates careless fighting; he prefers to win by craft."

sentences.chinese: 今戰既失利，而更逼賊者，必有由也。
sentences.literal: Now that battle has already gone badly, yet he presses the bandits harder—there must be a reason.
sentences.idiomatic: We have just tasted defeat, yet he drives harder at the foe—something drives him.

sentences.chinese: 」萇聞而謂碩德曰：「登用兵遲緩，不識虛實，今輕兵直進，逕據吾東，必苟曜豎子與之連結也。
sentences.literal: " Chang heard and said to Shuo De: "Deng moves his army slowly and does not read feint from fact; now light troops drive straight in and seize our east—it must be that brat Gou Yao has joined him."
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang heard and said to Shuo De: "Fu Deng is slow and blind to ruse; light horse now spear our eastern flank—that pup Gou Yao has tied his fate to Deng's."

sentences.chinese: 事久變成，其禍難測。
sentences.literal: If matters drag on until they ripen, the harm cannot be fathomed.
sentences.idiomatic: Let the knot tighten and the harm becomes unreadable.

sentences.chinese: 所以速戰者，欲使豎子謀之未就，好之未深，散敗其事耳。
sentences.literal: The reason I strike quickly is to catch the brat before his plot is finished and his fondness for it not yet deep, and scatter and ruin his affair.
sentences.idiomatic: I hit fast so the whelp's scheme never ripens, his commitment never deepens—I break the thing apart.

sentences.chinese: 」進戰，大敗之，登退屯於郿。
sentences.literal: " He advanced to battle, broke them utterly, and Deng withdrew to garrison at Mei.
sentences.idiomatic: He pressed the attack, shattered them, and Fu Deng fell back to entrench at Mei.

sentences.chinese: 登將金槌以新平降萇，萇輕將數百騎入槌營。
sentences.literal: Deng's general Jin Chui surrendered Xinping to Chang; Chang lightly led several hundred riders into Chui's camp.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng's general Jin Chui yielded Xinping; Yao Chang rode in with only a few hundred horse to Chui's lines.

sentences.chinese: 群下諫之，萇曰：「槌既去苻登，復欲圖我，將安所歸！
sentences.literal: His subordinates remonstrated. Chang said: "If Chui has left Fu Deng yet plots against me, where can he turn!"
sentences.idiomatic: His men protested. Yao Chang said: "If Jin Chui has quit Fu Deng only to knife me, where would he run?"

sentences.chinese: 且懷德初附，推款委質，吾復以不信待之，何以禦物乎！
sentences.literal: Moreover one newly come over in good faith has laid open trust and given hostage; if I meet him with distrust, how shall I govern the world!"
sentences.idiomatic: A new friend offers open heart and hostage; answer with suspicion and nothing in the realm will hold!"

sentences.chinese: 」群氐果有異謀，槌不從而止。
sentences.literal: " The band of Di indeed harbored a treacherous plot, but Chui would not follow it and it stopped.
sentences.idiomatic: The Di clique did plot treason, yet Chui refused—and the plot died.

sentences.chinese: 萇如陰密攻登，敕其太子興曰：「苟曜好奸變，將為國害，聞吾還北，必來見汝，汝便執之。
sentences.literal: Chang went to Yinmi to attack Deng and instructed his heir Xing: "Gou Yao loves treacherous shifts and will harm the state; when he hears I have turned north he is sure to come to you—then seize him."
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang marched on Yinmi against Fu Deng and told the crown prince Xing: "Gou Yao thrives on double dealing and will poison the realm. When he learns I have swung north he will seek you out—take him then."

sentences.chinese: 」苟曜果見興于長安，興遣尹緯讓而誅之。
sentences.literal: " Gou Yao indeed visited Xing at Chang'an; Xing sent Yin Wei to reproach him and put him to death.
sentences.idiomatic: Gou Yao called on Yao Xing in Chang'an; Xing sent Yin Wei to shame him, then executed him.

sentences.chinese: 萇大敗登于安定東，置酒高會，諸將咸曰：「若值魏武王，不令此賊至今，陛下將牢太過耳。
sentences.literal: Chang broke Deng utterly east of Anding, set a banquet, and the generals all said: "Had we met Wei Wuwang, this bandit would not have lasted until today; Your Majesty holds the reins too tight."
sentences.idiomatic: East of Anding Yao Chang crushed Fu Deng, then feasted his captains. They said: "Under Wei Wuwang this cur would never have lived so long; you keep too tight a hand, Majesty."

sentences.chinese: 」萇笑曰：「吾不如亡兄有四：身長八尺五寸，臂垂過膝，人望而畏之，一也；
sentences.literal: " Chang smiled and said: "I fall short of my dead elder brother in four things: he stood eight chi five cun tall, arms hanging past the knees—men saw him and feared him; first;
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang smiled: "I lack four gifts my dead brother had: eight chi five of height, arms past the knee—men quailed at the sight; one;

sentences.chinese: 當十萬之眾，與天下爭衡，望麾而進，前無橫陣，二也；
sentences.literal: facing a hundred thousand host, contending balance with All-under-Heaven, he advanced at a wave of the banner and never met a blocking line; second;
sentences.idiomatic: before a hundred thousand spears he matched the world, flag dipped and line moved—no shield could hold him; two;

sentences.chinese: 溫古知今，講論道藝，駕馭英雄，收羅雋異，三也；
sentences.literal: he warmed the ancient and knew the present, lectured on the Way and arts, drove heroes, and gathered the strange and excellent; third;
sentences.idiomatic: he knew old texts and the hour, discoursed on craft and principle, mastered captains and netted rare men; three;

sentences.chinese: 董率大眾，履險若夷，上下咸允，人盡死力，四也。
sentences.literal: he led great hosts, trod peril as if it were flat, won assent above and below, and every man gave his death strength; fourth.
sentences.idiomatic: he marched great armies through razor country as on a road, won every heart, and drew the last breath from every soldier; four.

sentences.chinese: 所以得建立功業，策任群賢者，正望算略中一片耳。
sentences.literal: The reason I could build merit and employ the host of worthies is that I hoped for one slice within calculation and strategy."
sentences.idiomatic: If I raised an empire and set able men to work, it was because I still had one thin edge of cunning left."

sentences.chinese: 」群臣咸稱萬歲。
sentences.literal: " The assembled officials all shouted "Long life!" thrice.
sentences.idiomatic: The court cried "May you live ten thousand years!"

sentences.chinese: 萇下書令留台諸鎮各置學官，勿有所廢，考試優劣，隨才擢敘。
sentences.literal: Chang issued an edict ordering each rear garrison to install study officials, forbid abolishing them, examine excellence and mediocrity, and promote according to talent.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang ordered every rear command to keep schools and masters, test for merit, and advance men by gift.

sentences.chinese: 苻登驃騎將軍沒奕于率戶六千降，拜使持節、車騎將軍、高平公。
sentences.literal: Fu Deng's Cavalry-in-Charge General Moyiyu led six thousand households to surrender; he was appointed Bearer of the Scepter, Chariots-and-Cavalry General, and Duke of Gaoping.
sentences.idiomatic: Moyiyu, Fu Deng's chief of horse, brought six thousand households over; Yao Chang gave him the staff, the chariots-and-horse command, and the ducal title of Gaoping.

sentences.chinese: 萇寢疾，遣姚碩德鎮李潤，尹緯守長安，召其太子興詣行營。
sentences.literal: Chang took to his bed; he sent Yao Shuo De to garrison Lirun, Yin Wei to hold Chang'an, and summoned his heir Xing to the field headquarters.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang fell ill; he posted Yao Shuo De at Lirun, left Yin Wei in Chang'an, and called Crown Prince Xing to camp.

sentences.chinese: 征南姚方成言於興曰：「今寇賊未滅，上復寢疾，王統、苻胤等皆有部曲，終為人害，宜盡除之。
sentences.literal: South-Conquering Yao Fangcheng said to Xing: "The bandits are not yet destroyed; the sovereign is ill again; Wang Tong, Fu Yin, and the like all have personal retinues—they will in the end harm men; they ought all to be removed."
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Fangcheng, who campaigned south, warned Xing: "Rebels still live; your father sickens again; Wang Tong and Fu Yin keep private hosts—they will turn venomous. Cut them clean."

sentences.chinese: 」興於是誅苻胤、王統、王廣、徐成、毛盛，乃赴召。
sentences.literal: " Xing thereupon executed Fu Yin, Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng, then answered the summons.
sentences.idiomatic: Xing killed Fu Yin, Wang Tong, Wang Guang, Xu Cheng, and Mao Sheng, then rode to his father.

sentences.chinese: 興至，萇怒曰：「王統兄弟是吾州裏，無他遠志，徐成等昔在秦朝，並為名將。
sentences.literal: When Xing arrived, Chang angrily said: "The Wang Tong brothers are men of my province; they harbor no distant ambition. Xu Cheng and the like were famed generals under Qin.
sentences.idiomatic: When Xing came, Yao Chang blazed: "Wang Tong and his brothers are home-country men with no larger design. Xu Cheng and his fellows were named generals of Qin.

sentences.chinese: 天下小定，吾方任之，奈何輒便誅害，令人喪氣！」
sentences.literal: The realm is settling; I was about to employ them—how could you slaughter them at will and make men lose heart!"
sentences.idiomatic: Peace is near and I meant to use them—why cut them down and drain the courage from every officer?"

sentences.chinese: 萇下書，兵吏從征伐，戶在大營者，世世復其家，無所豫。
sentences.literal: Chang issued an edict: soldiers and clerks who had followed expeditions, households registered in the great camp—generation after generation their families were exempted and bore no levy.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang decreed perpetual exemption for families of soldiers and scribes who had marched with the host and were tallied to the grand camp—no corvee would touch their line.

sentences.chinese: 苻登與竇沖相持，萇議擊之，尹緯言於萇曰：「太子純厚之稱，著于遐邇，將領英略，未為遠近所知。
sentences.literal: Fu Deng and Dou Chong stood locked; Chang deliberated striking them. Yin Wei said to Chang: "The heir's reputation for pure simplicity is known far and near; his martial brilliance as a leader is not yet known far and near.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng and Dou Chong were deadlocked; Yao Chang thought to strike. Yin Wei said: "The crown prince is famed for honest depth, but his steel as a commander is still a secret beyond the court.

sentences.chinese: 宜遣太子親行，可以漸廣威武，防窺窬之原。
sentences.literal: You ought to send the heir in person; thus you may gradually broaden martial awe and guard the root of creeping encroachment.
sentences.idiomatic: Send him in person—let awe spread step by step and choke off any thought of usurpation.

sentences.chinese: 」萇從之，戎興曰：「賊徒知汝轉近，必相驅入堡，聚而掩之，無不克矣。
sentences.literal: " Chang agreed; he instructed Xing: "When the bandits know you draw near, they will surely drive one another into forts; gather and ambush them, and none will stand."
sentences.idiomatic: " Yao Chang assented and briefed Xing: "Once they know you come, they will herd into their forts—ring and swallow them, and none escape."

sentences.chinese: 」比至胡空堡，沖圍自解。
sentences.literal: " When he reached Hukong Fort, Chong's siege dissolved of itself.
sentences.idiomatic: By the time he reached Hukong Fort, Dou Chong's ring had fallen away on its own.

sentences.chinese: 登聞興向胡空堡，引還，興因襲平涼，大獲而歸，咸如萇策。
sentences.literal: Deng heard Xing was bound for Hukong Fort and led his troops back; Xing thereupon raided Pingliang, took a great haul, and returned—all as Chang had planned.
sentences.idiomatic: Fu Deng heard Xing aimed at Hukong Fort and pulled back; Xing swept Pingliang for a rich prize and rode home—just as Yao Chang had drawn it.

sentences.chinese: 使興還鎮長安。
sentences.literal: He ordered Xing to return and garrison Chang'an.
sentences.idiomatic: He sent Xing back to hold Chang'an.

sentences.chinese: 萇下書除妖謗之言及赦前奸穢，有相劾舉者，皆以其罪罪之。
sentences.literal: Chang issued an edict striking demonic-slander speech and pre-amnesty vileness; whoever impeached another on those grounds was punished with the crime he alleged.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang voided charges of witch-slander and old filth pardoned by amnesty—any accuser who dredged them up wore the guilt he tried to pin.

sentences.chinese: 晉平遠將軍、護氐校尉楊佛嵩率胡蜀三千餘戶降于萇，晉將楊佺期、趙睦追之。
sentences.literal: Jin's Far-Smoother General and Di Protector Colonel Yang Fosong led more than three thousand Hu and Shu households to surrender to Chang; Jin generals Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu pursued him.
sentences.idiomatic: Yang Fosong, Jin's far pacifier and Di warden, led three thousand-odd Hu and Ba households to Yao Chang; Yang Quanqi and Zhao Mu of Jin gave chase.

sentences.chinese: 遣姚崇赴救，大敗晉師，斬趙睦。
sentences.literal: He sent Yao Chong to the rescue; he broke the Jin army utterly and beheaded Zhao Mu.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang sent Yao Chong; Jin's host shattered and Zhao Mu lost his head.

sentences.chinese: 以佛嵩為鎮東將軍。
sentences.literal: Fosong was made General Who Guards the East.
sentences.idiomatic: Yang Fosong became General Who Guards the East.

sentences.chinese: 萇如長安，至於新支堡，疾篤，輿疾而進。
sentences.literal: Chang went toward Chang'an; reaching Xinzhai Fort his illness turned grave, and he was carried forward while sick.
sentences.idiomatic: Yao Chang set out for Chang'an; at Xinzhai Fort his sickness bit deep, and they bore him onward on a litter.

sentences.chinese: 夢苻堅將天官使者、鬼兵數百突入營中，萇懼，走入宮，宮人迎萇刺鬼，誤中萇陰，鬼相謂曰：「正中死處。
sentences.literal: He dreamed Fu Jian leading envoys of the celestial office and several hundred ghost soldiers bursting into camp; Chang fled in fear into the palace; palace women met Chang and stabbed at ghosts, but wrongly struck Chang's privates; the ghosts said to one another: "Right in the death place.
sentences.idiomatic: He dreamed Fu Jian at the head of heaven's clerks and hundreds of wraith-troops storming the camp. Yao Chang ran to the inner hall; women struck at spirits and gashed his groin by mistake. The shades murmured: "Dead center.

sentences.chinese: 」拔矛，出血石餘。
sentences.literal: " They drew the spear; blood flowed more than a peck.
sentences.idiomatic: They pulled the lance free; blood ran more than a peck.

sentences.chinese: 寤而驚悸，遂患陰腫，醫刺之，出血如夢。
sentences.literal: He woke in terror and palpitation; then he suffered swelling of the privates; the doctor lanced it, and blood came as in the dream.
sentences.idiomatic: He woke shaking; the flesh swelled; the leech lanced it and the flood matched the vision.

sentences.chinese: 萇遂狂言，或稱「臣萇，殺陛下者兄襄，非臣之罪，願不枉臣。
sentences.literal: Chang then raved; sometimes he declared: "Your subject Chang—the one who killed Your Majesty was elder brother Xiang; it is not your subject's crime; I pray you do not wrong your subject.
sentences.idiomatic: Then Yao Chang raved, crying: "Lord, I am Chang—your killer was my brother Xiang, not I; do not call it my guilt.

sentences.chinese: 」至長安，召太尉姚旻、尚書左僕射尹緯、右僕射姚晃、尚書狄伯支等入，受遺輔政。
sentences.literal: " Reaching Chang'an, he summoned Grand Commandant Yao Min, Left Director Yin Wei, Right Director Yao Huang, Minister Di Bozhi, and others to enter and receive his dying charge to assist the government.
sentences.idiomatic: In Chang'an he called Yao Min, Yin Wei, Yao Huang, Di Bozhi, and the rest to take the deathbed regency.

sentences.chinese: 萇謂興曰：「有毀此諸人者，慎勿受之。
sentences.literal: Chang said to Xing: "If any slander these men, carefully do not believe it.
sentences.idiomatic: He told Xing: "Whoever blackens these men—do not lend your ear.

sentences.chinese: 汝撫骨肉以仁，接大臣以禮，待物以信，遇黔首以恩，四者既備，吾無憂矣。
sentences.literal: You soothe flesh-and-bone with benevolence, receive great ministers with ritual, treat affairs with good faith, and meet the black-haired commoners with grace—once the four are ready, I have no worry."
sentences.idiomatic: Rule kin with kindness, greet high ministers with rite, handle the realm with trust, meet the people with mercy—set those four and I rest easy."

sentences.chinese: 」乙太元十八年死，時年六十四，在位八年。
sentences.literal: In the eighteenth year of Taiyuan he died; at the time he was sixty-four; he had been on the throne eight years.
sentences.idiomatic: He died in the eighteenth year of the Taiyuan era, aged sixty-four, after eight years on the throne.

sentences.chinese: 偽諡武昭皇帝，廟號太祖，墓稱原陵。
sentences.literal: Posthumously he was titled Martial-and-Luminous Emperor, temple name Grand Progenitor, tomb called Yuanling.
sentences.idiomatic: They gave him the posthumous name Martial Luminous Emperor, the temple title Grand Founder, and buried him at the tomb called Yuanling.
